title: Best Kitchen Knives UK
short: Knife sets and individual chef's, santoku, paring and bread knives compared by sharpness, comfort and price.
intro: A good knife set covers most kitchen tasks, but a few individual specialist knives often outperform what comes in a block. This guide compares both, tested by Expert Reviews, from budget sets to knives with built-in sharpeners.

guide.q: Do I need a knife set or individual knives?
guide.a: A set covers most everyday tasks in one purchase and usually works out cheaper overall. Buying individual knives lets you choose the best option for each specific job, such as a dedicated paring or bread knife, but costs more to build a full collection.

Forged knives are made from a single piece of heated, shaped steel and tend to be heavier, more durable and better balanced. Stamped knives are cut from a sheet of steel, making them lighter and usually cheaper, though generally less long-lasting.

guide.q: Are built-in knife sharpeners worth it?
guide.a: A block with an integrated sharpener, like the Elevate Knives or Ninja sets here, keeps blades sharp with minimal extra effort or cost, though it takes some practice to use correctly and can add to the price.

guide.q: Can I put my kitchen knives in the dishwasher?
guide.a: Check each knife's care instructions individually, as it varies a lot even within a set. Dishwasher detergent and heat can dull blades and damage some handle materials, particularly wood, so many premium knives recommend hand-washing even if others in the same set are dishwasher safe.
